# goldenmatch_pg

> GoldenMatch entity resolution as a PostgreSQL extension (pgrx): score, dedupe,
> match, auto-config, a stateful identity graph, and the native blocking,
> profiling and semantic-layer kernels.

## Install

```sql
CREATE EXTENSION goldenmatch_pg;
```

Every function lives in the `goldenmatch` schema (the extension is not
relocatable), so call them qualified -- `SELECT goldenmatch.goldenmatch_score(...)`
-- or put `goldenmatch` on your `search_path`.

## Authoritative sources

Read these instead of inferring behaviour from the function signatures:

- https://docs.bensevern.dev/extensions/sql -- the SQL surface (Postgres + DuckDB).
- https://docs.bensevern.dev/llms.txt -- index of every Golden Suite surface.
- https://github.com/benseverndev-oss/goldenmatch -- source, issues, and the
  decision records behind the behaviour.

From inside a session: `SELECT goldenmatch.goldenmatch_docs();` returns this file.

## Function families

Roughly eighty functions. JSON in / JSON out wherever a scalar will not do.

- **Scoring** -- `goldenmatch_score`, `_score_pair`, `_explain`,
  `_score_probabilistic`, `_train_em`.
- **Dedupe / match** -- `goldenmatch_dedupe`, `_dedupe_table`, `_dedupe_pairs`,
  `_dedupe_clusters`, `_dedupe_full`, `goldenmatch_match`, `_match_tables`,
  `_match_pairs`.
- **Auto-config** -- `goldenmatch_autoconfig`, `_autoconfig_telemetry`,
  `_suggest_threshold`, `_detect_domain`, `_extract_features`.
- **Quality / evaluation** -- `goldenmatch_profile_table`, `_validate_table`,
  `_autofix_table`, `_detect_anomalies`, `_preflight`, `_postflight`, `_evaluate`,
  `_compare_clusters`.
- **Jobs** -- `gm_configure`, `gm_run`, `gm_jobs`, `gm_pairs`, `gm_clusters`,
  `gm_golden`, `gm_drop`, `gm_telemetry`.
- **Identity graph** -- reads `goldenmatch_identity_resolve`, `_view`, `_history`,
  `_conflicts`, `_list`; **writes** `gm_resolve`, `gm_identity_merge`, `_split`,
  `_claim`, `_resolve_conflict`; audit `gm_identity_audit`, `_audit_seal`,
  `_audit_verify`; MDM reads `gm_identity_profile`, `_stats`, `_worklist`.
- **Learning memory** -- `correction_add`, `correction_list`, `memory_learn`,
  `memory_stats`.
- **Native kernels (no embedded CPython)** -- `goldenmatch_hnsw_pairs`,
  `goldenmatch_lsh_pairs`, `goldenmatch_perceptual_phash` / `_hamming`,
  `goldenmatch_pair_dedup` / `_str`, `goldenmatch_connected_components` / `_str`,
  `goldenmatch_record_fingerprint`, `goldenmatch_embed_local`, `gm_embed`.
- **GoldenCheck profiling (native)** -- `goldencheck_benford`, `_near_duplicates`,
  `_discover_fds`, `_discover_approx_fds`, `_composite_keys`.
- **GoldenFlow transforms** -- eight `goldenflow_*` functions.
- **Semantic layer (native)** -- `goldenmatch_certify_structural`.

## Things that are decided, not incidental

- **Some functions run native-direct and some go through embedded CPython.**
  That split is deliberate and per-function: a kernel is de-bridged only once a
  byte-parity corpus proves the Rust path matches the Python reference. So
  `goldenmatch_score` on the four rapidfuzz-family scorers is pure Rust, while
  `soundex_match` / `ensemble` still call the bridge; `goldenflow_strip` is
  native, `goldenflow_normalize_phone` is not (its core kernel is NANP-only and
  therefore not a drop-in).
- **The native kernels are the SAME code as the DuckDB, wheel and WASM surfaces**
  -- one Rust kernel behind one shared golden fixture. `goldenmatch_hnsw_pairs`
  here and in DuckDB return byte-identical candidate pairs by construction.
- **Multi-column kernel arguments are column-major flat arrays plus an `n_cols`**,
  not `text[][]`. pgrx flattens multidimensional arrays, so the flat-array-plus-dim
  idiom is the workaround, not a design preference.
- **Identity writes are Postgres-only.** DuckDB has no durable multi-connection
  store, so it carries the five reads and nothing else. The write path here uses
  the `goldenmatch.identity_dsn` GUC (superuser-set) and opens a second libpq
  connection to that DSN.
- **The SQL is hand-maintained.** pgrx 0.12.9 does not generate it, so every
  `#[pg_extern]` must also appear in the base SQL for the current
  `default_version` -- enforced in CI by `scripts/check_pgrx_sql_sync.py`. A
  published version is immutable: a new function goes into the NEXT version's
  base plus a migration script, never retro-added to a released base.
- **A large slice of the Python API is intentionally NOT in SQL** -- PPRL,
  streaming, the LLM family, boost/rerank, graph ER, sensitivity sweeps. Each is
  deferred for a documented reason (file-path arguments, statefulness, network
  access, model downloads), not because nobody got to it.

## DuckDB counterpart

`goldenmatch-duckdb` exposes the same capabilities as Python UDFs, function for
function, so the two backends are interchangeable apart from the identity write
path described above.
